source.title: The Magic Correlations: Understanding Knowledge Transfer from Pretraining to Supervised Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Si-Min Fan; Dimitris Paparas; Natasha Noy; Binbin Xiong; Noveen Sachdeva; Berivan Isik

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses scaling laws and the use of small proxy models, but its experiments measure benchmark accuracy and confidence transfer from pretraining to SFT across data mixtures. They do not test held-out cross-entropy scaling, loss extrapolation across run sizes, compute-optimal allocation, architecture effects, or the claim versions listed.
record.gate_note: The scaling-law results in the related-work section are cited background, not results from this study. The paper's own cross-stage benchmark correlations are adjacent evidence about pretraining-to-SFT transfer, not measurements of the claimed scaling laws; recorded below as findings that fit no version. No scaling-law claim versions are tested.
record.test_reason: The study trains 240M and 1B models on 9 data mixtures. It correlates pretraining benchmark accuracy and confidence with post-SFT values across mixtures. It fits no loss-scaling law and reports no held-out loss, extrapolation or compute allocation. V6 needs downstream performance predicted by scale or pretraining loss. Here the predictor is pretraining benchmark accuracy across data mixtures at two scales, a different construct. Kaplan and Hoffmann appear only as background and as motivation for proxy-model practice.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, but it should also say this. Transfer from pretraining to SFT depends on capability category and benchmark. Accuracy and confidence transfer move in opposite directions with scale: accuracy transfer is stronger at 1B, confidence transfer weaker. Data-curation effects seen at 240M (e.g. FineWeb-Edu on NLI) can reverse at 1B, so the authors advise validating data choices at multiple scales.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses correlations of benchmark accuracy and confidence across training stages and data mixtures, rather than fitting loss-scaling laws or finding compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported transfer patterns vary with model scale, capability category, benchmark, data mixture, and training stage.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean PT→SFT accuracy correlation across mixtures is 0.49 at 240M and 0.59 at 1B (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How well pretraining benchmark rankings predict post-SFT rankings varies with model scale and benchmark category.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean PT→SFT confidence correlation is 0.66 at 240M and 0.41 at 1B (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-stage persistence of confidence weakens with scale even as accuracy persistence strengthens.

fits_no_version.finding: FineWeb-Edu vs RefinedWeb NLI accuracy effect reverses between scales: +5.0pp at 240M, -4.4pp at 1B (Table 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-mixture effects on benchmark accuracy measured on small proxy models may not carry over to larger models.

record.problems: Only two model scales are tested, and the study uses one SFT dataset and protocol. Aggregate correlation values differ across sections of the paper. These limitations concern the study's adjacent transfer analysis, not direct evidence on scaling laws.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-law results are reported by this study. Benchmark-specific transfer values and other data-mixture analyses were not extracted because they do not measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: No held-out loss is measured against parameters, tokens or compute; only two model sizes are trained.
No power-law fit and no extrapolation of loss to larger runs.
No comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fits for fine-tuning or other regimes; SFT is studied only via cross-stage correlations.
No downstream performance is predicted from scale or pretraining loss. Accuracy is correlated across training stages and data mixtures, at two sizes only.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits are compared across setups.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given because no version is tested. The study cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as background. Its proxy-model caution concerns benchmark accuracy under data-mixture changes at two scales, not loss extrapolation. The paper's internal numbers are inconsistent (Finding 7 vs Table 5, and Figure 2's caption). The appendix says 22 benchmarks in 8 categories, while the main text says 20 in 4.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Predicting larger-run loss from power-law fits to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.
Effects of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law scaling outside ordinary text pretraining or under other training regimes.
Downstream performance prediction from scale or pretraining loss; the study instead measures accuracy correlations across pretraining and SFT data mixtures.
Dependence of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices.
